lessons.title: Pre-mixing and Wetting of Pigments
lessons.body: Pre-mixing is where you combine the pigment powder with the liquid ingredientsâresin, solvent, and additivesâto form a paste. The goal is to wet every pigment particle with liquid, so they don't clump together. In Africa, many small paint factories use a high-speed disperser (also called a mixer) for this step. A typical batch starts with 200 liters of alkyd resin in a 500-liter stainless steel tank. Turn on the disperser at low speed (around 500 rpm) and slowly add 150 kg of titanium dioxide powder. If you dump it in too fast, you get lumps that are hard to break later. Add the pigment over 10â15 minutes while the mixer runs. Then add 20 liters of mineral turpentine to adjust viscosity, and 5 kg of dispersing agent (like a polyacrylate) to help the particles separate. After all pigment is in, increase speed to 1500 rpm for 20â30 minutes. The mixture should look like a smooth, thick cream. Check the temperatureâit should not exceed 50Â°C. If it gets too hot, reduce speed or add a little solvent. In hot African climates, you may need to cool the tank with a water jacket or work in the early morning. Wetting is not just mixing; it's a chemical process where the liquid replaces air on the pigment surface. A good pre-mix will save you time and energy in the milling stage. Always wear a dust mask and goggles when handling pigment powders.

lessons.title: Dispersion Techniques and Equipment Operation
lessons.body: Dispersion means breaking apart pigment clusters (agglomerates) and spreading them evenly in the liquid. After pre-mixing, you need to apply high shear force. The most common equipment in African paint workshops is the high-speed disperser (HSD) with a saw-tooth blade. The blade diameter should be about one-third of the tank diameter. For a 500-liter tank, use a 150-mm blade. Set the blade height so it is about one blade diameter from the bottomâthis creates a rolling vortex. Start at low speed (500 rpm) to avoid splashing, then increase to 2000â3000 rpm. The tip speed should be around 15â20 meters per second. At this speed, you will see a whirlpool and hear a characteristic whine. Disperse for 30â45 minutes. For harder pigments like iron oxide, you may need a bead mill or a triple-roll mill. A bead mill uses small ceramic beads (1â2 mm) to grind particles. In a small factory, a horizontal bead mill with a 20-liter chamber can process 100 liters per hour. Always check the ammeter on the motorâif it draws too much current, you are overloading the mill. Reduce feed rate or increase bead load. In Africa, power fluctuations can damage motors, so use a voltage stabilizer. Clean equipment immediately after use; dried paint is very hard to remove. Use a solvent like xylene or acetone. Safety: never open a running mill; beads can fly out. Keep a fire extinguisher nearby because solvents are flammable.

lessons.title: Milling and Particle Size Reduction
lessons.body: Milling reduces pigment particles to their final size, usually 5â20 microns. Smaller particles give better color strength, gloss, and stability. After dispersion, the paste may still have particles larger than 50 microns. You need a mill to grind them down. In Africa, three types of mills are common: ball mill, bead mill, and triple-roll mill. A ball mill is a rotating cylinder with steel or ceramic balls. It is slow (12â24 hours) but cheap and good for hard pigments. A bead mill is faster (1â2 hours) and uses small beads. A triple-roll mill has three rollers that squeeze the paste; it is good for viscous pastes but requires skill. For a small paint factory, a bead mill is often the best choice. For example, a 30-liter bead mill with 1.5-mm zirconia beads can grind a 100-liter batch in 2 hours. The feed rate should be about 10 liters per minute. Check the particle size with a Hegman gauge (see next lesson). You want a reading of 6â7 on the gauge (which means 15â25 microns). If it's lower, run the mill longer or reduce feed rate. Milling generates heat, so cool the mill with water. In hot climates, monitor temperature; if it exceeds 60Â°C, stop and cool. After milling, the paste is called 'mill base' and is ready for let-down. Always wear ear protectionâmills are noisy.

lessons.title: Monitoring Dispersion Quality: Hegman Gauge
lessons.body: The Hegman gauge (also called a grind gauge or fineness of grind gauge) is a simple stainless steel block with one or two grooves. The groove depth goes from 100 microns at one end to 0 microns at the other. You place a drop of paint in the deep end and draw a straight-edged scraper down the groove. The point where you see specks or scratches indicates the particle size. The scale is marked 0 to 8, where 8 means 0 microns (perfectly smooth) and 0 means 100 microns. For most architectural paints, you want a Hegman reading of 5â7 (which is 20â40 microns). For automotive or high-gloss paints, you need 7â8 (0â10 microns). To use the gauge, clean it with solvent and a soft cloth. Place a few drops of the mill base at the deep end. Hold the scraper perpendicular and pull it down smoothly in 1â2 seconds. Immediately look at the groove under good light. Note the scale number where you first see a speck. Do this three times and take the average. In Africa, where dust is common, always cover the gauge between uses. If your reading is too low (e.g., 3â4), your dispersion is poor. You may need to add more dispersing agent, increase milling time, or check for worn beads. A good Hegman reading saves you from producing paint that settles or looks gritty. Keep a record for each batch.

lessons.title: Let-Down and Final Mixing
lessons.body: Let-down is the step where you add the remaining resin, solvent, and additives to the mill base to turn it into finished paint. The mill base is thick and concentrated; you need to dilute it to the right viscosity and pigment volume concentration (PVC). For a typical emulsion paint, you might have 200 kg of mill base. In a large mixing tank, add 300 kg of resin (e.g., acrylic emulsion) and 100 kg of water. Start the mixer at low speed (300 rpm). Slowly add the mill base. Then add 20 kg of coalescing agent, 5 kg of defoamer, and 10 kg of thickener. Mix for 30â45 minutes until uniform. Check viscosity with a flow cup (Ford cup #4). For brush application, aim for 20â25 seconds. Adjust with water or thickener. Add biocides (2 kg) to prevent spoilage in hot climates. Also add colorants if needed. For solvent-based paints, use a similar process with solvent instead of water. Always add the mill base to the let-down tank, not the other way around, to avoid shocking the emulsion. After mixing, let the paint stand for 1 hour to release air bubbles. Then check pH (should be 8â9 for emulsion). If pH is low, add ammonia. This step is critical for consistency. In Africa, many small factories skip proper let-down and get lumpy or separated paint. Take your time.

lessons.title: Filtration and Packaging
lessons.body: After let-down, the paint may contain small lumps, dried skin, or foreign particles. Filtration removes these to give a smooth product. Use a nylon filter bag or a vibrating screen. For small batches, a simple bag filter with 50â100 micron mesh works well. Place the bag in a drum or over a tank. Pour the paint through the bag. For larger batches, use a basket mill or a self-cleaning filter. In Africa, many factories use a mesh screen (80â120 mesh) stretched over a frame. Change the filter when the flow slows down. After filtration, the paint is ready for packaging. Fill into clean containersâplastic buckets (5L, 20L) or metal tins. Use a filling machine or a simple gravity filler. Weigh each container to ensure accurate fill. For 20L buckets, fill to 20 kg (assuming density ~1.0). Seal the lid tightly with a rubber mallet. Label with product name, batch number, date, and color. Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. In hot African climates, avoid storing in metal containers that can rust. Always keep a sample from each batch for quality control. Clean all equipment immediately with water (for emulsion) or solvent (for solvent-based). Proper filtration and packaging prevent customer complaints and returns.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of pre-mixing in paint production?
options: A) To grind pigment particles to final size
B) To wet pigment particles with liquid and form a paste
D) To adjust the final viscosity
quiz.explanation: Pre-mixing combines pigment with liquid to wet particles and create a uniform paste before dispersion.

quiz.q: Which equipment is most commonly used for pre-mixing in small African paint factories?
quiz.explanation: High-speed dispersers are versatile and widely used for pre-mixing and dispersion in small-scale operations.

quiz.q: What should you do if the pre-mix temperature exceeds 50Â°C?
options: C) Reduce speed or add solvent
quiz.explanation: Reducing speed or adding solvent helps cool the mixture and prevents overheating.

quiz.q: What is the recommended blade diameter for a high-speed disperser in a 500-liter tank?
quiz.explanation: The blade diameter should be about one-third of the tank diameter, so 150 mm for a 500-liter tank.

quiz.q: What tip speed is typical for dispersing pigments with a high-speed disperser?
quiz.explanation: A tip speed of 15â20 m/s provides sufficient shear to break agglomerates without excessive wear.

quiz.q: Which mill is best for grinding hard pigments like iron oxide in a small factory?
quiz.explanation: Ball mills are slow but effective for hard pigments and require less maintenance.

quiz.q: What is the typical grinding time for a bead mill to process a batch?
quiz.explanation: Bead mills are fast, typically reducing particle size in 1â2 hours.

quiz.q: What should you check if the ammeter on a bead mill shows high current?
options: C) Reduce feed rate or increase bead load
quiz.explanation: High current indicates overloading; reducing feed rate or adjusting bead load can help.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of milling in paint production?
options: A) To mix pigment with resin
B) To reduce pigment particle size
quiz.explanation: Milling reduces pigment particles to their final size, improving color and stability.

quiz.q: What is a typical particle size achieved after milling for architectural paint?
quiz.explanation: Most architectural paints require particles in the 5â20 micron range for good performance.

quiz.q: What does a Hegman gauge measure?
quiz.explanation: The Hegman gauge measures the fineness of grind, indicating particle size.

quiz.q: What Hegman reading is desired for most architectural paints?
quiz.explanation: A reading of 5â7 corresponds to 20â40 microns, suitable for architectural paints.

quiz.q: How should you clean a Hegman gauge?
options: A) With water and a wire brush
B) With solvent and a soft cloth
quiz.explanation: Solvent and a soft cloth prevent damage to the precision grooves.

quiz.q: What does a low Hegman reading (e.g., 3â4) indicate?
quiz.explanation: A low reading means large particles remain, indicating poor dispersion.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of let-down in paint production?
options: B) To dilute mill base and add remaining ingredients
quiz.explanation: Let-down adjusts viscosity and pigment concentration by adding resin, solvent, and additives.

quiz.q: In what order should you add ingredients during let-down?
options: A) Mill base first, then resin
B) Resin first, then mill base
quiz.explanation: Adding mill base to the let-down tank slowly prevents shocking the emulsion.

quiz.q: What viscosity (Ford cup #4) is typical for brush-applied emulsion paint?
quiz.explanation: 20â25 seconds gives good brushability for most emulsion paints.

quiz.q: Why is biocide added during let-down?
options: B) To prevent spoilage in hot climates
quiz.explanation: Biocides inhibit bacteria and fungi growth, especially important in warm, humid conditions.

quiz.q: What pH range is typical for emulsion paint after let-down?
quiz.explanation: Emulsion paints are usually alkaline, with pH 8â9 for stability.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of filtration in paint production?
options: A) To remove lumps and foreign particles
quiz.explanation: Filtration ensures a smooth product by removing oversized particles.

quiz.q: What mesh size is common for filtering paint in small factories?
quiz.explanation: 50â100 mesh filters are effective for removing lumps without slowing production too much.

quiz.q: How should you fill a 20L bucket of paint?
options: A) Fill to 20 liters by volume
B) Fill to 20 kg by weight
quiz.explanation: Paint is typically sold by weight, so 20 kg for a 20L bucket (density ~1.0).

quiz.q: What should be included on a paint container label?
options: A) Product name and batch number
quiz.explanation: Labels must include product name, batch number, date, and color for traceability.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep a sample from each batch?
options: A) For quality control and troubleshooting
quiz.explanation: Retained samples help identify issues if customer complaints arise.

quiz.q: What is the recommended mixing speed during let-down?
quiz.explanation: Low speed (300â500 rpm) prevents air entrapment and splashing during let-down.

quiz.q: What additive helps release air bubbles after let-down?
quiz.explanation: Defoamers reduce surface tension and allow air bubbles to escape.

quiz.q: What is the consequence of skipping proper let-down?
quiz.explanation: Improper let-down can lead to poor dispersion, lumps, and phase separation.

quiz.q: What should you do if the Hegman gauge reading is too low after milling?
options: B) Increase milling time or add dispersing agent
quiz.explanation: Poor dispersion may require more milling or additional dispersing agent to reduce particle size.

quiz.q: Why is it important to clean equipment immediately after use?
options: A) To prevent dried paint from hardening
quiz.explanation: Dried paint is very difficult to remove and can contaminate future batches.

quiz.q: What safety precaution is essential when handling pigment powders?
options: A) Wear a dust mask and goggles
quiz.explanation: Pigment powders can be harmful if inhaled or contact eyes, so protective gear is necessary.
